battle.name: 馬科曼尼戰爭
battle.brief: 安提奧庫斯四世洗掠耶路撒冷聖殿、禁絕猶太教之後，祭司馬塔提亞在摩底因起兵，率民兵抗塞琉古。猶大·馬卡比以夜襲、伏擊與山地遊擊擊破三名塞琉古將領的遠征軍，迫尼加諾戰死於車原平原，前 160 年重獻聖殿。卡面的斯巴達長矛未曾上陣，它代表塞琉古方陣長槍的族譜：此戰說明方陣站不住。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries:
馬科曼尼戰爭是前 167／166 年起、猶太地區反抗塞琉古王國的武裝起義，交戰雙方分別是安提奧庫斯四世治下的塞琉古帝國中央軍，以及由祭司馬塔提亞率領的猶太義軍。塞琉古一方以安提阿的宮廷為中樞，國王安提奧庫斯四世（伊庇法涅）坐鎮都城，向外派任總督與將軍：耶路撒冷周邊由提摩太管治，阿克辣要塞由駐軍把守，戰役層面則由尼加諾、戈爾吉亞斯與呂西亞斯率領的遠征隊與圍城大軍擔任。塞琉古是亞歷山大留下的馬其頓王國之一，軍制以希臘化方陣為核心：長槍方陣居中，弓箭手與輕步兵兩翼配合，騎兵護住側翼，象兵列於前鋒，另有攻城塔、撞槌與填壕的工程隊，以及大量受薪的雇傭兵。聖殿被劫掠之後，安提奧庫斯把猶太置於西頓總督與米涅拉俄斯的直接管轄之下，禁絕猶太祭祀、割禮與安息日，改以希臘風俗治理，並在聖殿聖地安置偶像。
猶太一方起初只是安提奧庫斯王權下的一個稅區，首義並無建制軍隊。馬塔提亞原是耶路撒冷祭司利未支派的後人，住在鄉村摩底因；地方上另有哈西德人結社，首義時與馬卡比家族約定結盟聯手作戰，才形成一支共同的武裝。義軍的骨幹是哈西德人與各村的鄉村步兵，祭司與利未人負責糧秣、聖器與後勤，無成建制騎兵，也沒有攻城器械；其作戰依托猶太山地的隘口、村落、旱井與窖藏，取糧多靠劫取敵軍糧道與奪回被徵空的村寨。
countriesEn:
The Maccabean War was an armed revolt that broke out in Judea in 167/166 BCE against the Seleucid Empire of Antiochus IV Epiphanes. On the Seleucid side stood the central army of the imperial court at Antioch: the king himself, appointed satraps and generals, the governor of the Judean district, and the garrison of the Akra citadel inside Jerusalem, with the field forces given over to commanders such as Nicanor, Gorgias and Lysias. The Seleucid state was one of the successor kingdoms of Alexander the Great, and its army was built around the Hellenistic phalanx: a long-pike phalanx in the centre, archers and light infantry working the flanks, cavalry covering the wings, elephants in front, supported by siege engineers with towers, battering rams and ditch-filling crews, plus a large body of paid mercenaries. After the Temple of Jerusalem was looted, Antiochus put Judea under the direct authority of the satrap of Sidon and of Menelaus, forbade Jewish worship, circumcision and the Sabbath, governed through Hellenic custom, and set up an idol on the Temple mount.
On the Judean side there was at first no regular army at all: the revolt was raised by a priest and a group of village militias. Mattathias, a descendant of the Levitical priestly house of Joarib who lived in the village of Mod'in, was joined at the outset by the Hasideans, who concluded a compact with the Maccabean family to fight together, and only thus did a common armed force come into being. Its backbone was the Hasideans and the foot-soldiers of the villages, while priests and Levites handled grain, cult vessels and logistics. There was no organised cavalry and no siege train; everything depended on the passes, villages, wells and cisterns of the Judean hills, on raiding enemy supply lines and on retaking villages that had been drained of their produce.
people:
起義的關鍵人物是祭司馬塔提亞（馬塔提亞·約翰之子、西門之孫，出自祭司利未家族 Joarib 支派）與他的五個兒子：猶大·馬卡比、約拿單·亞弗、西門·塔西，以及約拿單與以利以謝。塞琉古紀年 145 年、前 166 年的冬天，馬塔提亞在摩底因殺死那位登上祭壇褻瀆的「不敬之人」，公開拒絕服從安提奧庫斯的命令；義軍由他率領到冬季結束，不久他病逝，猶大·馬卡比接過指揮，是全戰役中戰術最成熟、影響最大的人物。約拿單在哥哥陣亡後主持大局，並於前 161 年派使團到羅馬，是猶太人第一次以邦交身分面對地中海強權。西門在戰役尾聲及戰後數年鞏固成果，前 152 年成為不受塞琉古節制的大祭司。
敵方方面，國王安提奧庫斯四世是推動全面希臘化的關鍵人物；他先以雅頌取代俄尼亞斯三世，又用重金賄賂換得大祭司職的米涅拉俄斯同樣不得人心。前 170 年安提奧庫斯在埃及貝魯斯提姆受阻後急需錢財，遂於前 167 年洗掠聖殿，把聖器熔鑄或運往安提阿，激發全猶太的抵抗。將領之中，戈爾吉亞斯在埃瑪烏斯被夜襲，呂西亞斯圍耶路撒冷而不得下，尼加諾兩度敗績，最終戰死車原平原。祭司以利以謝在貝特匝加里亞之役主動撞擊象兵陣而死，後世尊之為殉道者；約瑟夫斯在《古代史》第十二卷中為這批人物留下了最詳細的敘述。
peopleEn:
The key figure of the revolt was the priest Mattathias, son of John and grandson of Simeon, of the priestly house of Joarib, together with his five sons: Judas Maccabeus, Jonathan Apphus, Simon Thassi, and John and Eleazar. In the winter of Seleucid year 145, 166 BCE, Mattathias killed at Mod'in the apostate who had climbed the altar and desecrated it, and openly refused to obey Antiochus's orders; he led the rebel force until the end of that winter and then died of illness, and Judas Maccabeus took over command, proving himself the most accomplished tactician and the most consequential man of the whole war. Jonathan took charge after his brother's death and in 161 BCE sent an embassy to Rome, the first time the Jews appeared before a Mediterranean great power as a diplomatic partner. Simon consolidated the gains at the end of the fighting and in the years after it, becoming high priest in 152 BCE free of Seleucid control.
On the enemy side, King Antiochus IV was the decisive author of the policy of forcible Hellenisation; he first displaced Onias III in favour of Jason and then, through heavy bribery, put Menelaus into the high priesthood, which pleased nobody. After his Egyptian advance was checked at Pelusium in 170 BCE and he needed money in haste, he sacked the Temple in 167 BCE, melting down and carrying off its vessels to Antioch, and so set the whole of Judea ablaze. Among his commanders, Gorgias was surprised by a night attack at Emmaus, Lysias failed to take Jerusalem, and Nicanor was beaten twice before dying on the Plain of the Chariots. The priest Eleazar deliberately charged the line of elephants at Beth Zechariah and was killed, and later tradition honours him as a martyr; Josephus in the twelfth book of his Antiquities preserves the fullest narrative of all these men.
kits:
卡面上是斯巴達長矛（Dory）：一柄約兩米長的木槍，前端裝鐵矛頭，槍尾帶一枚青銅套尾，供士兵插在地上支撐盾牌，並在近身纏鬥時作反擊與支槓之用。斯巴達重裝方陣講究沿正面疊盾前推，槍尖越過盾緣層層探出，這一整套體系都以這支矛為核心，所以它被稱為「先決定誰站得住」的兵器。
然而這場戰爭裡，沒有任何一方真正打過希臘式方陣。塞琉古帝國的步兵用薩里薩長槍（sarissa），即方陣長槍，長度遠超兩米，是同一族譜上更晚、更重的變體；配合大盾、整齊的方陣線與象兵前鋒，構成安提奧庫斯四世賴以遠征的骨幹。猶太義軍則完全相反：他們沒有重甲，長矛多為鄉土削製、無銅套尾的普通矛，主要用於刺擊而非支盾；他們真正倚重的是投射兵器——弓與投石索，《馬卡比二書》15:20-22 稱投石索為「馬卡比家的戰馬」，說他們擲出的石如手中握石之投石者。攻城一方，塞琉古備有攻城塔、撞槌與填壕的工程隊，義軍則無任何攻城器械，改以封鎖、斷糧與夜襲消耗敵軍。補給線上，塞琉古靠安提阿至地中海沿岸的道路與海運供應，義軍靠猶太山地的村落、井與窖藏，取糧多自敵軍糧道奪回。斯巴達長矛的影子只在塞琉古一方的軍制裡，作為它象徵的方陣傳統；義軍手中同樣形制的長矛，則從未排成過一面盾牆。
kitsEn:
On the card is the Spartan dory: a wooden spear about two metres long, with an iron head at the front and a bronze butt-spike at the rear, planted in the ground to prop a shield and used in close fighting both to parry and to make room for the body. The Spartan phalanx was built on the principle of advancing in a solid front with shields overlapped, spears projecting layer upon layer beyond the shield rims, and the whole system centred on this one weapon; it is therefore the piece that decided, before the sword, who would be the one still standing.
Yet in this war neither side ever fought a proper Greek phalanx. The Seleucid foot carried the sarissa, the phalanx pike far longer than two metres and a later, heavier member of the same family; together with the large shield, the disciplined phalanx line and the elephants in front, it formed the backbone of Antiochus IV's campaigns. The Judean insurgents were the exact opposite: they had no heavy armour, their spears were mostly plain country shafts without a bronze butt-cap, meant for stabbing rather than for propping shields, and what they really relied on were missile weapons, bow and sling. Second Maccabees 15:20-22 calls the sling the battle-horse of the Maccabees and says they flung their stones like a man hurling a stone from his hand. On the siege side the Seleucids had towers, battering rams and crews for filling ditches, while the insurgents had no siege engine of any kind and used blockade, cutting of food supplies and night attacks to grind the enemy down instead. On the supply line the Seleucids drew provisions from the road and the sea transport between Antioch and the Mediterranean coast, while the insurgents lived off the villages, wells and cisterns of the Judean hills and took their grain back from the enemy's supply columns. The shadow of the Spartan dory survives only in the Seleucid order of battle, as the token of a phalanx tradition; the spears of the same form in the hands of the insurgents were never once set in a wall of shields.
tactics:
塞琉古方的戰術框架是希臘化王國的標準模式：以方陣正面展開，騎兵護兩翼，弓箭手與輕步兵在陣前試探，接著全線推壓；圍城時以封鎖替代強攻，用工程隊慢慢填壕、破門。但安提奧庫斯四世的遠征隊多與主力分開，糧道長，士氣不穩，一旦在陌生山地遭襲便各自崩潰。
義軍的戰術完全為地形與人數量身訂造。其一是拒絕正面方陣：猶大從不與塞琉古主力正面對撞，只在隘口、溪谷與山脊交戰。其二是夜襲與襲營，最典型的是埃瑪烏斯之夜的破營，猶大得知戈爾吉亞斯大軍駐紮後自側翼突入，殺傷二千餘人，並奪得敵方的營壘、兵器與糧秣。其三是設伏截斷退路，義軍在溪谷上方的斜坡埋下伏兵，待敵軍騎兵進谷再斷其後路，殲滅八百人，使敵軍全營潰散。其四是追擊的教訓，埃瑪烏斯之戰義軍放走了潰退之敵，遂遭反擊而受挫，直到學會窮追猛打，才把戰果坐實。
攻守兩面，義軍沒有攻城器械，也不強攻阿克辣要塞，而是長期封鎖其糧水、掘壕、夜襲出擊，逼得塞琉古統帥不得不撤圍；直到前 152 年西門時代才以斷絕糧道與談判迫使要塞放棄。軍紀上，首義時哈西德人與馬卡比家族立約結盟，後世傳統記下「休整一日再出戰」的安排；而守安息日與節齋期不動兵的宗教紀律，既是士氣來源，也限制了追擊與夜戰的節奏，這在《馬卡比一書》2:29-31 正是爭議的焦點。
tacticsEn:
The Seleucid tactical template was the standard one of the Hellenistic kingdoms: the phalanx deployed in front, cavalry covering the flanks, archers and light infantry probing ahead, and then a general advance along the whole line; when besieging, they preferred blockade to assault, filling the ditch and breaking the gate by slow engineering work. But Antiochus IV's field columns usually operated detached from the main army, with long supply lines and shaky morale, and once they were struck in unfamiliar hill country they fell apart on their own.
The insurgents built a doctrine entirely suited to their terrain and their numbers. First, they refused the frontal phalanx: Judas never met the Seleucid main force head-on, and fought only at passes, in wadis and along ridges. Second, they used the night attack and the assault on a camp; the clearest case is the breaking of Gorgias's camp at Emmaus, where Judas learned where the great army lay, came in on the flank by night and killed more than two thousand men, taking the enemy's camp, weapons and baggage. Third, they ambushed the retreat: the insurgents posted themselves on the slope above the wadi, let the enemy cavalry ride into the ravine, then cut the line behind them and destroyed eight hundred men, collapsing the whole camp. Fourth, they learned the lesson of pursuit; after Emmaus they let the broken enemy escape and suffered a counterblow, and only after learning to follow the fuggers and finish them did the victories become permanent.
On both the offensive and the defensive side the insurgents had no siege engines and did not storm the Akra citadel; they blockaded its food and water, dug in, and made night sallies until the Seleucid commander had to lift the siege, and it was only in Simon's time, in 152 BCE, that cutting the supply route and negotiating brought the fortress to surrender. On discipline: at the outset the Hasideans entered into a compact with the Maccabean family, and later tradition records the arrangement that the force would rest for a single day and then fight; and the religious observance of the Sabbath and of festival fasts, which forbade fighting, was both a source of morale and a limit on the rhythm of pursuit and night action. That tension is precisely what 1 Maccabees 2:29-31 is arguing about.
data:
先記時間。依《馬卡比一書》的塞琉古紀年（自前 312／311 年起算），前 166 年為紀年 145 年，前 164 年為紀年 148 年，前 161 年為紀年 150 年。起義爆發於前 166 年冬、猶太曆赫舍萬月二十三日（Cheshvan 23），約當公曆十二月初；聖殿重獻於前 164 年基斯流月二十五日；最激烈的一段落在前 165 至前 161 年之間，猶大遇刺在前 160 年。
再記兵力與消耗。《馬卡比一書》3:57 記埃瑪烏斯之戰戈爾吉亞斯部約二千人陣亡；3:58 記其軍為五千步兵與一千騎兵，義軍一方則自稱「人數不多」；4:40 記溪谷伏擊斬首八百人；《馬卡比二書》12:34 記一次戰役斬敵約五千；13:2-4 記尼加諾率八百騎兵追擊義軍時反被包圍全殲。約瑟夫斯《古代史》第十二卷亦記塞琉古遠征軍以萬計，並記安提奧庫斯四世在埃及受阻後靠洗掠聖殿變賣器物填補軍費，約九千名被擄的猶太人與祭司被押往王國各地安置。
最後記距離與地理。摩底因在耶路撒冷西北約三十公里，埃瑪烏斯在城西約二十公里，貝特匝加里亞在城南約八公里，艾都崙與貝特霍巴一帶的曠野在城南偏西，約旦河谷與死海東岸是義軍的南方退路；《馬卡比二書》12:31 記義軍在「沙庫谷地」一線扎營，學者多認為在死海東南的阿拉巴河谷附近，但具體對應仍存爭議。攻城方面，耶路撒冷聖殿山上的阿克辣要塞自前 163 年起遭封鎖隔絕，前 152 年方告陷落，圍困延續近十年。
dataEn:
First the chronology. On the Seleucid era used in 1 Maccabees, counted from 312/311 BCE, 166 BCE is Seleucid year 145, 164 BCE is year 148, and 161 BCE is year 150. The revolt broke out in the winter of 166 BCE, on the twenty-third day of Cheshvan, roughly the beginning of December in the civil calendar; the Temple was rededicated on the twenty-fifth of Kislev in 164 BCE; the fiercest phase of the fighting lies between 165 and 161 BCE, and Judas was assassinated in 160 BCE.
Next, the numbers of men and of losses. 1 Maccabees 3:57 records that about two thousand of Gorgias's men fell at Emmaus; 3:58 gives his force as five thousand foot and a thousand horse, while the insurgents describe themselves as a company not many in number; 4:40 records eight hundred killed in the ambush in the wadi; 2 Maccabees 12:34 records about five thousand enemy dead in one engagement; and 13:2-4 records Nicanor pursuing the insurgents with eight hundred horsemen only to be surrounded and destroyed. Josephus in the twelfth book of the Antiquities likewise describes Seleucid expeditionary armies numbering in the thousands and more, and records that after being checked in Egypt, Antiochus IV met his military costs by selling off the Temple vessels, with about nine thousand Jewish captives, priests among them, carried off to various parts of the kingdom.
Last, distances and geography. Mod'in lies about thirty kilometres north-west of Jerusalem, Emmaus about twenty kilometres west of the city, Beth Zechariah about eight kilometres to the south, the wilderness around Adullam and Beth-hoba to the south and west, and the Jordan valley and the eastern shore of the Dead Sea form the insurgents' southern line of retreat. 2 Maccabees 12:31 records the insurgents pitching camp in the plain of the Sacor, which most scholars place near the Arabah valley south-east of the Dead Sea, though the exact identification remains disputed. On sieges: the Akra citadel on the Temple mount in Jerusalem was blockaded and isolated from about 163 BCE and did not fall until 152 BCE, a siege that dragged on for close to ten years.
cause:
塞琉古方面，安提奧庫斯四世接手的是一個以希臘化為表面、以王權財政為實際的帝國：他急於把安提阿的秩序推展到各行省，同時在前 170 年進攻埃及失利，又在前 167 年返軍途中需要大筆錢財。耶路撒冷聖殿的器物因此成了他眼中的財源，洗掠之後，殿內的金器被熔鑄與運走，祭司被殺，祭司長職被出賣給出錢最多的人。
宗教與族群層面的衝突更為根本。猶太教與希臘化城市生活方式並不兼容，安提奧庫斯禁止割禮、禁止守安息日、禁止研讀《申命記》，在聖殿聖地安置偶像，又把耶路撒冷改稱「安提阿」，等於宣告一位真神的聖殿可以被另一套神聖秩序取代。地方層面，摩底因的官員在盟長面前強娶希伯來寡婦、拆毀婚約，馬塔提亞正是為此拔刀——這是全猶太在聖殿被掠之後壓抑怒氣的導火線。
更遠的背景是塞琉古王位繼承的混亂。安提奧庫斯四世先後排斥兄弟與姪兒，其政策欠缺政治上的正當性；全面希臘化並非他一人發明，但在他手上變成了不計後果的鎮壓。於是本來只是稅區的猶太，在聖殿被掠之後被推入全面起義。
causeEn:
On the Seleucid side, Antiochus IV had inherited an empire that was Hellenistic in appearance and fiscal in substance: he was in a hurry to extend the order of Antioch to the provinces, and at the same time he had been checked in Egypt in 170 BCE and needed a great deal of money on his return in 167 BCE. The vessels of the Temple of Jerusalem were therefore money in his eyes. After the sack, the gold of the sanctuary was melted down and carried off, the priests were killed, and the office of high priest was sold to the man who could pay the most.
The conflict was deeper still on the religious and ethnic level. Judaism and the Hellenistic manner of life in the cities were incompatible; Antiochus forbade circumcision, forbade the keeping of the Sabbath, forbade the reading of Deuteronomy, set up an idol on the Temple mount, and renamed Jerusalem Antiochia, thereby declaring that the sanctuary of the one true God could be replaced by another sacred order. At the local level, an official of Mod'in took a Jewish widow by force before the elders and broke her marriage contract, and it was for that act that Mattathias drew his sword; it was the fuse that released the anger held by all Judea after the desecration of the Temple.
The deeper background was the disorder of the Seleucid succession. Antiochus IV had successively pushed aside his brothers and his nephew, and his policy lacked political legitimacy; the wholesale Hellenisation was not his invention, but in his hands it became a repression that counted no cost. And so a Judea that had been merely a tax district, once the Temple had been looted, was driven into open revolt.
impact:
這場戰爭的產物是一個新王朝。塞琉古帝國在安提奧庫斯四世於前 164 年死後迅速崩解，兒子安提奧庫斯五世在位僅四個月，帝國分裂為安提奧克與帕提亞兩部分；本已被塞琉古王權壓制多年的猶太，趁這個空隙建立起以哈斯蒙尼家族為核心的自治政權。前 161 年猶大·馬卡比派使團赴羅馬，取得元老院「羅馬人民之友與盟友」的稱號，這是猶太人第一次以外交條約的身分出現在羅馬的文獻中。
宗教與文化層面的影響更為持久。聖殿在戰爭中被破壞又被重獻，祭司祭祀恢復，重獻之日的基斯流月二十五日後來成為哈努卡節（光明節）的由頭，今天全球猶太家庭仍以這場戰爭作為不屈抵抗的象徵；體育界自 1932 年起舉辦的「馬卡比亞運動」（Maccabiah）亦以此命名。在基督宗教傳統裡，馬卡比一書、二書長期被列入天主教正典，馬卡比兄弟被視為抵抗迫害的聖徒典範。
但這場戰爭也留下了長期分裂的種子。北方「塞拉古派」指責馬卡比家族過於世俗化、擁護異教王朝，等到前 167 年以後他們另立旗幟，這條血統線最終演成「馬卡比派」與「法利賽派」的分黨；而馬卡比家族建立的王朝本身也很快陷入內鬥，希律崛起、哈斯蒙尼王朝於前 37 年被羅馬廢黜，正是這段歷史的下游。
impactEn:
The product of this war was a new dynasty. The Seleucid Empire fell apart quickly after the death of Antiochus IV in 164 BCE; his son Antiochus V ruled for only four months, and the empire split into an Antiochene and a Parthian half. Judea, so long held down by the Seleucid crown, used the opening to build a self-governing polity centred on the Hasmonean house. In 161 BCE Judas Maccabeus sent an embassy to Rome and obtained from the Senate the title of friend and ally of the Roman people, and it was the first time the Jews appeared in Roman documents in the person of a treaty partner.
The religious and cultural consequences proved even more durable. The Temple was destroyed in the war and then rededicated, priestly worship was restored, and the twenty-fifth of Kislev on which it was rededicated became the origin of the festival of Hanukkah, or the Feast of Lights; families of the Jewish diaspora today still keep this war as the image of stubborn resistance, and the Maccabiah games first held in 1932 take their name from it. In the Christian tradition, the First and Second Books of Maccabees long stood in the Catholic canon, and the Maccabee brothers were honoured as a model of saints who resist persecution.
Yet the war also sowed the seeds of a lasting split. The northern Hellenists, the so-called Seleucid party, accused the Maccabees of being too worldly and too attached to a pagan dynasty, and once they set up their own standard after 167 BCE this bloodline quarrel developed into the division between the Maccabees and the Pharisees; and the dynasty the Maccabees founded itself soon fell into civil war, with the rise of Herod and the Roman deposition of the Hasmoneans in 37 BCE forming the downstream end of this history.
result:
就戰役本身而言，結果是清楚的：安提奧庫斯四世時期的鎮壓體制被推翻，聖殿重獻、祭祀恢復，耶路撒冷的阿克辣要塞被隔絕近十年後於前 152 年落入手中，猶太人第一次建立了自己的武裝與能與強權交涉的外交。塞琉古一方則失去了地中海沿岸走廊上最難啃的一個行省；安提奧庫斯四世死後，新王安提奧庫斯五世曾經出兵，於前 160 年擊敗約拿單、迫他退讓，說明戰爭並未一勞永逸地解決宗主權問題，猶太人直到西門與其子孫那一代，才真正取得不必再聽命於安提阿的地位。
人物的下場同樣說明戰爭的走向。猶大·馬卡比於前 160 年在耶利哥附近的堡壘被其姻親托勒密暗殺，隨後由約拿單接手；約拿單於前 143 年被托勒密殺死，西門最後於前 141／140 年在耶利哥的宴席上被毒殺，兄弟三人無一善終。他們留下的不是穩固的王位，而是一支能打的軍隊與一套聖殿祭祀的秩序。
回到卡面：斯巴達長矛所代表的那一面盾牆，恰恰是這場戰爭裡失敗者的形狀。塞琉古帝國有最完整的方陣、最雄厚的兵員與最遠的補給線，仍然輸給一群不穿甲、不排方陣、靠山地與節奏作戰的起義者。戰爭之後，猶太人再沒有回到希臘式方陣的傳統，而馬卡比的名字被記住的原因，也正在於他們拒絕讓那支矛決定誰站得住。
resultEn:
As far as the fighting itself goes, the outcome is plain: the apparatus of repression built under Antiochus IV was broken, the Temple was rededicated, worship was restored, the Akra citadel in Jerusalem passed into Jewish hands in 152 BCE after almost ten years of isolation, and the Jews acquired for the first time both an armed force of their own and a foreign policy of their own. The Seleucids in turn lost the most difficult province on the Mediterranean coastal corridor. After the death of Antiochus IV, the new king Antiochus V did send out troops and defeated Jonathan in 160 BCE, forcing him to give ground, which shows that the war did not settle the question of suzerainty in one stroke; it was only in the generation of Simon and his sons that the Jews obtained a position that no longer required them to take orders from Antioch.
The fates of the principals tell the same story. Judas Maccabeus was murdered in 160 BCE in a fortress near Jericho by his kinsman Ptolemy, and was succeeded by Jonathan; Jonathan was killed by Ptolemy in 143 BCE, and Simon was finally poisoned at a feast in Jericho in about 141/140 BCE, so that none of the three brothers met a natural end. What they left behind was not a secure throne but a field army that could fight and a restored order of Temple worship.
Back to the card: the wall of shields that the Spartan dory stands for is precisely the shape of the loser in this war. The Seleucid Empire had the most complete phalanx, the heaviest manpower and the longest supply lines in the field, and it still lost to a band of insurgents who wore no heavy armour, formed no phalanx, and fought with the hills and the rhythm of the fighting. After the war the Jews did not go back to the Greek phalanx tradition, and the reason the name of the Maccabees was remembered is precisely that they refused to let that spear decide who would be the one still standing.
